info.bio: Emerson, Lake & Palmer (también conocida como ELP) fue una banda inglesa de rock progresivo que alcanzó su mayor popularidad en década de 1970, vendiendo más de 35 millones de discos y realizando multitudinarios conciertos. La espectacularidad de sus grabaciones y presentaciones los pusieron a la altura de las grandes bandas de hard rock y heavy metal de los setenta. scenes.name: Rock progresivo
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Al emigrar a Gran Bretaña, el rock se convierte en mercancía de moda pero también se descontextualiza: lo que en EE UU era el diario de la juventud se vuelve en Gran Bretaña un ensayo. El progresivo no comenta la cultura juvenil sino que busca la innovación técnica: arranca con las óperas rock (S.F. Sorrow, Tommy) y los álbumes conceptuales, lo cimentan Traffic, Jeff Beck, Jethro Tull, Family y Genesis, y alcanza su cima con King Crimson (In The Court Of The Crimson King), Van Der Graaf Generator y Yes. Colosseum, la Third Ear Band (inventores de la world music), las variantes góticas (High Tide, Black Widow) y folk (Comus, Strawbs), Gentle Giant, Emerson Lake & Palmer y Roxy Music, que revoluciona el género y prepara la new wave y el synth-pop.

podcast.title: Artwork Designer
podcast.body: H.R. Giger, known for creating the Xenomorph in the "Alien" movie franchise, also designed album artwork for Emerson, Lake & Palmer. "HR Geeger, the guy who created the Xenomorph for the alien movie franchise, also got into the album artwork business. He did stuff for Emerson Lincoln Palmer, Debra Harry, and the Dead Kennedys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Counter-Movement Inspiration
podcast.body: The qualities of "lugubrious, intricate, wady" music, which progressive rock fans prized in ELP's sound, were precisely what the emerging artists like the "Angry Young Men" were striving to counteract with their back-to-basics approach. "The very things that progressive rock fans prized in the music of ELP, Yes, Pink Floyd and Early Genesis. These were what the musicians I'm going to focus on today were trying to counteract."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Early Synthesizer Integration
podcast.body: As a prominent progressive rock band, Emerson Lake & Palmer were among the groups that actively dabbed in synthesizers during the 1970s, integrating these new electronic instruments into their complex musical structures. "There were plenty of Prague rock bands dabbling in synths. Emerson Lycan Palmer and yes were just two."
